chapter: Big bands, small groups and studio work
title: Black musicians on the CBS staff

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I want to get back a step to when you were hired on CBS. Were Emmett Barry and Billy Taylor and George Johnson hired the same time you were?
Same time, same time, the four of us.
So the contractor, did you get a feeling from him that he was sticking his neck out in hiring black musicians?

Well yes, and then they were trying to get that thing going there, John Hammond, so you didn't think too much about it, you know, because it wasn't any sort of prejudice or anything else evident up there when you were playing, because they all treated you beautiful. See Raymond, and then all the guys in the band, you know, just everybody up there just treated you wonderful, so you didn't feel that pressure at all.
I guess around the same time that you guys were doing that in New York, Lee Young was going through a similar thing in Hollywood.
Yeah, but that was afterward, though, wasn't it? Wasn't that after?
No I think it was the early '40s.

'43, around there. That was in, you know like in the big movie studios where they were doing all of the sound track recordings. So I guess it happened on both coasts around the same period. But, let's, since you mentioned Emmett Barry, you've known him for a long time.
